chunks: From him, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding the man who drags his garment, he said: 'I dislike that he resembles the women.'

key_terms.يَجُرُّ: drags (specifically of a garment trailing on the ground)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on men dragging their clothes and why?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) links the dislike of a man dragging his garment to the specific concern of imitating women, distinguishing this from the general prohibition of *israf* (extravagance) or pride. This narration, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tashabbuh* (gender-specific imitation) as a key criterion for evaluating male attire and modesty.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran,
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding the man who dragged his clothes: ‘I dislike it if one resembles with the women’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following: “About the case of a man who was dragging his clothes behind him on the ground, abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘I dislike one’s making himself look like a woman.’”
